votes.reason: At 16.2x trailing with EPS up 13.4%, the largest US bank is sound and fairly priced for its earnings growth, which is why I picked it.

At 16.2x trailing, tied with JPM for the lowest multiple on the sheet, this profitable biotech is still growing EPS (+3.0%), so it is cheap, and a 6.84% 12-week return shows the price has not run far ahead of that value.

27.1x trailing is the highest multiple on the sheet, but for a sound staple growing EPS 10.6% with 2.92% weekly volatility that is a full price rather than a concrete flaw, and it carries the staples call I made through PEP.
18.3x trailing on EPS up 45.2% is a modest multiple for that much earnings growth at a sound franchise, so even after an 18.77% 12-week run it is not expensive.

At 22.2x trailing, the second-highest multiple on the sheet, with EPS down 26.1%, this is paying up for shrinking earnings: the price relies on a recovery the numbers do not yet show and leaves no margin of safety.
